 View Comments Expect plenty of physicality from Tanner Jeannot and the Bruins in a rivalry game against the Canadiens. Matthew J. Lee/Globe Staff The rivalry between the Bruins and Canadiens takes on a new flavor Thursday when the Bruins don their new “Varsity Sweaters” for the first time. 
 The Bruins are drawing inspiration from Boston’s college hockey roots with their ongoing “Causeway University” campaign. They’re calling Thursday’s matchup a “homecoming game” and will host the Northeastern band — something Charlie McAvoy is especially excited about . 
 The Bruins will wear an all-brown uniform for the first time since the organization’s inaugural season in 1924 as they take on Montreal. Montreal is also wearing its “Hometown Remix” uniform, which Cole Caufield had quite the reaction to . 
 The two teams sit at the top of the Atlantic Division. The Bruins are on a four-game winning streak and the Canadiens enter riding an 11-game point streak (8-0-3). The Bruins are 8-1-0 at home and the Canadiens are 6-1-1 on the road. 
 Get Sports Alerts The latest sports news and Globe's most interesting reporting and commentary right to your inbox. Enter Email Sign Up Marco Sturm has faced Montreal as a player and coach in Boston. He is well aware of the rivalry’s nature. 
 “Actually, I just got a question from a friend of mine [this week], ’What’s your biggest rivalry?’ And I said, ’It’s still Montreal, for sure.’ Not even close,” Sturm said. “What I experienced even last year, that hasn’t changed. I’m really looking forward to [Thursday’s] game.” 
 Boston is 9-1-0 with a plus-22 goal differential in its last 10 games when playing Montreal on home ice. 
 The Bruins are kicking off a four-game homestand. 
 Related : Finally summoned from Providence, Mikey Eyssimont didn’t waste any time getting on the scoresheet for the Bruins Here’s a preview of Thursday’s game: 
 When: Thursday, 7 p.m. 
 Where: TD Garden, Boston 
 TV: NESN. Radio: WBZ-FM 98.5. 
 Line: Boston -125. O/U: 6.0. 
 CANADIENS 
 Season record: 11-3-4. vs. spread: 8-10. Over/under: 11-7 
 Last 10 games: 7-0-3. vs. spread: 6-4. Over/under: 5-5 
 BRUINS 
 Season record: 13-4-1. vs. spread: 14-4. Over/under: 7-10, 1 push 
 Last 10 games: 7-2-1. vs. spread: 8-2. Over/under: 3-6, 1 push 
 TEAM STATISTICS 
 Goals scored: Montreal 60, Boston 67 
 Goals allowed: Montreal 55, Boston 41 
 Power play: Montreal 14.8%, Boston 18.3% 
 Penalty minutes: Montreal 208, Boston 256 
 Penalty kill: Montreal 77.8%, Boston 77.0% 
 Faceoffs won: Montreal 52.8%, Boston 55.6% 
 Stat of the day: Morgan Geekie has also in four straight games (2 goals, 4 assists) after entering that stretch with just one goal this season. 
 Notes: The Canadiens have been whistled for 84 minor penalties, the second most in the league behind Florida’s 86. ... Jacob Fowler, recalled from AHL Laval a week into the season, owns a stellar 8-1-2 record and ranks third in the NHL with a .925 save percentage. ... Fowler will feel right at home in the Causeway University homecoming game after playing collegiately at Boston College.
